questions.prompt: Which Navy player is the net-front reference?
questions.explanation: F1 is the Navy player positioned near the net-front lane.

questions.prompt: Which two checks shape the point decision?

options.text: Whether F1 still screens a useful lane
Whether F2 is reachable across the slot
The point role alone chooses the release without a lane check

questions.explanation: Screen quality and the cross-slot connection shape the decision after the defender shifts.

Checking Gold 1/F1's screen and comparing F2 as a cross-slot option can overlap as YOU scan the ice; neither check has to finish before the other starts. The net-side lane still gets one last look right before the release, because pressure or the screen can still shift in that instant.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a different point angle relative to F1's screen.
questions.explanation: This changes the shooting line's angle without clearing F1's screen; the cross-slot option to F2 stays part of the picture too.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 opens the point but F1 moves away from the crease. What deserves attention?

options.text: Compare F2 or a protected release with the lost screen
Release through the former lane before checking F1’s screen
Assume the lane is still fully screened without rechecking

questions.explanation: The defender and screen both changed, so the next choice depends on the new support picture.

questions.prompt: What makes feedback on a point release useful in this rep?
questions.explanation: Name Gold 1, F1 and F2, then explain how their lanes affect a release, pass or protected reset. The screen cue can disappear before the choice.
